Fact.Name: Tax Exempt Interest
Fact.Description:
Form 1040 line 2a. The Add sums four legs: the Form 1099-INT box-8 total, per report floored at box 9 and net of the box-13 tax-exempt bond premium (/interestReports/*/taxExemptInterest); the Form 1099-DIV box-12 exempt-interest dividend total (dividendReports:/exemptInterestDividends); the Schedule K-1 (Form 1065) box 18 code A / Schedule K-1 (Form 1120-S) box 16 code A share of tax-exempt interest (/k1TaxExemptInterest); and the Form 1099-OID tax-exempt legs - box 2 when classified tax-exempt and box 11, each net of its own acquisition or bond premium - through /taxExemptOriginalIssueDiscountTotal. One instruction block names the box-8 and box-12 legs and routes them to the same printed line: "your tax-exempt stated interest should be shown in box 8 of Form 1099-INT ... Enter the total on line 2a of your Form 1040 or 1040-SR" and "Also include on line 2a of your Form 1040 or 1040-SR any exempt-interest dividends from a mutual fund or other regulated investment company. This amount should be shown in box 12 of Form 1099-DIV" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sb.pdf, page 2).
DIRECTION. Line 2a is read by eitc:/belowEitcInvestmentIncomeLimit (the IRC 32(i) disqualified-investment-income test), socialSecurity:/appendixBWorksheet3ProvisionalIncome and /socialSecurityBenefitsWkshtLine7 (the benefit-taxability base) and ptc:/ptcMagi. Understating any of the four legs would admit an EITC claimant who should be disqualified and shrink the SSB and MAGI bases.
COMPLETENESS: none of the three legs beside box 8 adds an Incomplete surface. dividendReports:/exemptInterestDividends and /k1TaxExemptInterest are each an IsComplete Switch with a $0 tail, complete safe on a return that carries no /dividendReports or /formK1s key and on records that leave the relevant box unanswered; /taxExemptOriginalIssueDiscountTotal's per-item guard blocks only a listed Form 1099-OID record missing its own box 2 amount, tax-exempt classification, or box 11 amount. This fact is Complete $0 on an ordinary 1099 with no boxes, and INCOMPLETE when a box-8 amount is present with the report's ../has1099 unanswered, because the box-8 leg's own guard is undiluted by the Add.
ROUNDS ONCE, AT THE LINE. Every leg besides the box-8 leg is unrounded in its own module, so this Round is the only one; a rounded term there would round twice. California TY2025 reads this fact through its stateSystems export (Schedule CA (540), Schedule CA (540NR)).

Fact.Name: This K-1's tax exempt interest income (box 18 code A / box 16 code A)
Fact.Description:
THIS Schedule K-1's share of the tax exempt interest income Form 1040 line 2a carries: the total of the rows whose printed letter code is A on Schedule K-1 (Form 1065) box 18 (tax exempt income and nondeductible expenses) and on Schedule K-1 (Form 1120-S) box 16 (items affecting shareholder basis). Both instructions route code A to the same printed line in the same words, "Individual partners include this amount on Form 1040 or 1040-SR, line 2a" and "Individual shareholders include this amount on Form 1040 or 1040-SR, line 2a".
THE TWO BOXES ARE READ TOGETHER AND CANNOT DOUBLE COUNT. Unlike the AMT items box, which is one row list for both K-1 layouts, box 18 and box 16 are TWO row lists in scheduleE (../taxExemptIncomeAndNondeductibleExpenseEntries for the partnership box, ../itemsAffectingShareholderBasisEntries for the S corporation box). A given K-1 item is one entity's document and fills one of the two lists, so summing both lists reads each recorded K-1 exactly once.
COMPLETE SAFE: a row contributes only when BOTH its code and its amount are answered and the code is the letter A, so a K-1 item that answered no box 18 or box 16 row contributes a Complete $0 and the CollectionSum over the collection stays Complete.
WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT ROUTED. Form 1065 box 18 codes B (other tax exempt income) and C (nondeductible expenses) and Form 1120-S box 16 codes B through E (other tax exempt income, nondeductible expenses, distributions, loan repayments) are BASIS ONLY: the instructions tell the partner or shareholder to adjust the basis of the interest or stock and, for code B, "don't include it in income on your tax return". This dictionary tracks no outside basis, so those rows stay intake only. Form 1120-S box 16 code F (foreign taxes paid or accrued) is NOT routed to Form 1116 because the instruction bars it in terms. Summed over the collection by /k1TaxExemptInterest.

A leg on the printed line but not on the test that chooses the arm would let the two disagree.
THE GATE IS THE COLLECTION, NOT /claimsEstateTrustK1, and that is a deliberate divergence from scheduleE:/estateTrustGrossFarmingFishingIncome. Line 2b IS taxed, so dropping a recorded box 1 because the filer never answered /writableHasEstateTrustK1 would understate income; the collection being non empty is the fact that matters here. Recorded for the lead rather than left to inference.
COMPLETE SAFE: the CollectionSum sits inside an IsComplete Switch on the /form1041K1s collection defaulting to $0, and each item's term defaults to $0, so a return that never opened the estate or trust K-1 section resolves Complete $0. Every committed scenario is byte identical: none answers box 1.
UNROUNDED, because both arms of /interestIncome already Round once at the line.

Fact.Name: Interest income
Fact.Description: Taxable interest income to report on line 2b of Form 1040. Both arms of the Switch below, and /requiresScheduleB, take the same set of addends beside the Form 1099-INT and Form 8958 terms: the Schedule K-1 box 5 / box 4 interest (scheduleE:/k1PortfolioInterestIncome, complete-safe $0 for every non-K-1 return), per the partner instructions ("Report interest income on Form 1040 or 1040-SR, line 2b."); /estateTrustK1InterestIncome, the Schedule K-1 (Form 1041) box 1 total, whose routing is printed on the form itself ("1. Interest income Form 1040 or 1040-SR, line 2b"); and form8912:/form8912AdditionalInterestIncome, the tax credit bond interest the Form 8912 credit is treated as - the credit allowed for a tax credit bond is included in gross income as interest, so the amount the filer has not already been sent a payee statement for is taxable interest on line 2b. Taking every addend on both arms and on /requiresScheduleB means the printed line, the arm that prints it and the test that chooses the arm can never disagree. Each addend is complete-safe $0 on a return that carries none of it, so every committed scenario is byte identical. The Form 1041 K-1 term is a single whole-dollar-rounded aggregate rather than a per-payer rounded Schedule B line-1 entry (a sub-dollar presentation simplification, never a tax understatement beyond the same rounding every aggregate carries).

Fact.Name: Schedule B printed line 2: add the amounts on line 1, before the series EE and I exclusion
Fact.Description:
The amount the printed Schedule B carries on LINE 2, "Add the amounts on line 1" - the line-1 payer subtotal and every other line-1 term this dictionary carries, less the below-the-subtotal line-1 adjustments, and BEFORE the line 3 series EE and I savings bond exclusion. Its whole job is the face of the form: line 2 less line 3 is line 4, and line 4 is /interestIncome, which is what the register prints at line 4 and what Form 1040 line 2b states.
WHY IT EXISTS. The register bound printed line 2 to /interestIncome, the POST-exclusion figure, and bound the SAME fact again at line 4. On a return claiming the section 135 exclusion the printed form therefore contradicted itself: line 2 and line 4 both showed the post-exclusion total while line 3 showed a positive exclusion, so line 2 less line 3 did not equal line 4 and line 2 was understated by exactly the exclusion. No tax figure moved - line 4 and Form 1040 line 2b were and are correct - but the printed schedule did not foot. THIS IS THE TWIN OF THE PRINTED LINE 4, NOT A NEW COMPUTATION. It is /interestIncome's own two-arm Switch, its GreaterOf $0 and its single Round, copied term for term with ONE deletion: the form8815:/form8815ExcludableSavingsBondInterestOrZero subtrahend, which is line 3 and belongs below line 2 and not inside it. The Schedule B arm is therefore selected by the SAME guard, /requiresScheduleB, that selects the arm printing line 4, so the two printed lines can never be computed on different routes. The /scheduleBLine1AdjustmentTotal subtrahend is KEPT, because this dictionary puts the nominee, accrued-interest and previously-reported-savings-bond subtractions above line 2 exactly as the line-1 instruction describes; the printed line-1 entries stay the payers' gross figures.
WHY NOT /interestIncomeBeforeForm8815Exclusion, which is arithmetically the same sum. That fact is the phaseout-independent MAGI basis, and its own Description says it "is not itself the Form 1040 line 2b amount". Its Schedule B arm is selected by /requiresScheduleBForForm8815Magi, a different predicate built to stay acyclic for the Form 8815 phaseout, and nothing measures that it agrees with /requiresScheduleB on every return. Binding a printed line to it would make the face of the form depend on a guard chosen for a cycle-avoidance reason, and a future divergence would silently print the non-Schedule-B arm on a printed Schedule B. The printed line reads the printed guard.
WHY NOT /interestIncome PLUS THE EXCLUSION. /interestIncome is floored at $0, so on any return where the floor binds, adding line 3 back would print a line 2 that overstates the line-1 subtotal by the whole exclusion.
FOOTING, STATED EXACTLY. Line 2 is GreaterOf $0 of Round(S), line 4 is GreaterOf $0 of Round(S less line 3), for the same S. The two agree exactly whenever line 3 is a whole-dollar amount, which is every return whose Form 8815 line 14 falls on a dollar; when line 14 carries cents the two printed lines can differ by at most $1, the residue of the single rounding each printed line carries, and the form's own whole-dollar convention is what creates it. The $0 floor is a second, narrower residue, stated rather than claimed away: the excludable interest on line 3 is part of the savings bond interest line 1 reports, so S is never smaller than line 3 EXCEPT where the signed Form 1099-INT boxes 10 to 12 term inside S drives it there on its own - $700 of line-1 interest, $200 of it qualified savings bond interest and $600 of box 11 premium gives S of $100 against a line 3 of $200, and line 4 floors to $0 while line 2 prints $100. That is the same filer the FLOORED AT $0 comment on /interestIncome already calls out as holding a Form 1099-INT the payer instruction says cannot be issued, and no committed fixture reaches it.
NOT /scheduleBLine4TotalTaxableInterest's sibling. That fact sums the UNROUNDED per-payer taxable interest and rounds once at the total, because it is the $1,500 threshold test; this fact sums the ROUNDED per-payer line-1 entries the schedule actually prints, exactly as /interestIncome's Schedule B arm does.

Fact.Description:
Whether any of the 1099-INT forms have a required FACTA filing box checked
NARROWED. The sentence above is the guard's whole original Description, kept verbatim; it used to be the guard's whole body too, so every filer one of whose payers checked the FATCA box was refused. It now refuses only when that box is checked on a 1099 report AND the return's Form 8938 threshold answer is ABOVE or UNANSWERED, read from the form8938 home module's pair form8938:/form8938ThresholdAnswered and form8938:/form8938AboveReportingThreshold. WHAT IS FREED: the filer with a checked FATCA box whose total specified foreign financial assets are BELOW the threshold that applies to them, the common case, since the lowest printed pair starts at $50,000 and one Form 1099-INT account says nothing about the total. WHAT STILL REFUSES, two arms: (a) ABOVE the threshold, because a Form 8938 must accompany the return and this dictionary does not produce one, a build gap; (b) the threshold question UNANSWERED with the box checked, the asked-and-not-answered residue, which is the correct permanent refusal: no figure on the form answers it and $0 is not a safe stand-in for an unknown asset total. THE TRAP THE CONTRACT NAMED IS AVOIDED BY CONSTRUCTION: this guard reads the return-level PAIR and never form1099Rs:/specifiedForeignFinancialAssetsAboveForm8938Threshold, whose box-12 gate makes it Complete FALSE, "below", on a return with a 1099-INT FATCA box and no 1099-R at all. Read that alias here and a filer who was never asked would file. THE ASK GATE IS THE GUARD'S OWN FIRST CONJUNCT, unchanged: a box answered TRUE on a report whose ../has1099 is answered TRUE, both IsComplete first, so an unanswered collection or an unanswered box still short-circuits to FALSE and nothing here becomes Incomplete. NO COMMITTED RETURN MOVES: no fixture or scenario answers a 1099-INT FATCA box true, so the guard is Complete FALSE everywhere before and after, the refused arms by facta-box-true-threshold-unanswered-still-refused (which also pins the form1099Rs alias Complete FALSE on the same return, the trap made visible) and facta-box-true-aggregates-above-threshold-still-refused.

Fact.Name: (Writable) Is this payer's interest community income?
Fact.Description:
THE PER-ITEM CHARACTER INPUT, and it is the whole difference between this unit and the wages unit that supplied its shape. Form 8958 splits wages with no state law qualifier, but it qualifies interest by its SOURCE: "Interest, dividends, and rents. Interest, dividends, and rents from" continuing "community property are community income and must be evenly" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f8958.pdf, page 3, LEFT column of a two column extraction; the RIGHT column at those lines is the self employment tax paragraph). Interest from SEPARATE property is not automatically separate either: "Income from separate property. In some states, income from" continuing "separate property is separate income. Other states characterize" (same file, lines 121 and 122, RIGHT column). So the question a filer can answer is the one the form itself puts to them — is this payer's interest community income under YOUR state's law — and not a question about the underlying account that this dictionary would then have to characterise for them.
NO DEFAULT, DELIBERATELY, and this is the direction that matters. An unanswered character makes ../isCommunityIncome FALSE, which leaves the item UNALLOCATED (its whole amount stays on this return) and leaves ../secondaryFilerUsedWithoutMFJ REFUSING when the item is the spouse's. Fail closed: this dictionary never assumes community.

Fact.Description:

AN ANSWERED FALSE AND AN UNANSWERED CHARACTER ARE THE SAME HERE AND DIFFERENT AT THE GUARD. Both leave the item unallocated. They part company at ../secondaryFilerUsedWithoutMFJ, which keeps refusing the spouse's item in BOTH cases — deliberately, because a spouse's SEPARATE income has no line on this return at all, which is the same input contradiction the guard was opened for.

Fact.Name: Form 8958 line 2 — the community half of this payer's interest that this unit moves
Fact.Description:
The taxpayer's allocated share of ONE Form 1099-INT's taxable interest, on a return that must allocate community income AND on an item the filer has characterised as community income. $0 on every other item and on every other return.
CENTS ARE NOT PRESERVED HERE AND THE FACT SAYS SO ON ITSELF (the wages unit's review lesson — a disclosure that lives only in the records is not a disclosure). MEASURED: Multiply(Rational 1/2, Dollar) rounds at the CENT, HALF EVEN. 700.01 allocates 350.00, not 350.005, because 350.005 rounds to the EVEN cent; 1,600.00 allocates 800.00; 4,000.00 allocates 2,000.00; 2,000.01 allocates 1,000.00 on the dividend twin. TWO BOUNDED CONSEQUENCES, disclosed rather than smoothed. (1) On an odd cent COMMUNITY row the two halves can miss Form 8958's own footing rule, "amounts in columns B and C. Together, columns B and C should" / "equal column A." (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f8958.pdf, page 4, LEFT column), by one cent. THAT ONE CENT IS A STATEMENT ABOUT A COMMUNITY ROW AND NOTHING ELSE: it is NOT the gap between this fact and column B on a mixed collection, which is the whole of the taxpayer's own separate income and is a different quantity entirely — see the paragraph below. (2) The cent miss is at most half a cent per item and cannot accumulate into a dollar on Form 1040 line 2b without more than 200 payers. Neither is fixable inside the dictionary: the engine's rounding mode is engine behaviour.
NOT ROUNDED TO THE DOLLAR, though: this is an addend of the Form 1040 line 2b chain and that line rounds once, at its own printed line.
THIS IS NOT COLUMN B ON EVERY ROW. Form 8958 column A holds "Enter the total amount of your community or separate income," (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f8958.pdf, page 4, LEFT column of a two column extraction) — SEPARATE income goes on the form too — and the columns must foot: "amounts in columns B and C. Together, columns B and C should" / "equal column A." (lines 201 and 202, LEFT column). So on a SEPARATE property row owned by this taxpayer, column A is the whole amount and column B is the whole amount, with column C zero. This fact is $0 on such a row. It is therefore the COMMUNITY HALF THIS UNIT MOVES, not the column B figure, and on a MIXED collection the two differ by the whole of the taxpayer's own separate income — not by a cent. THE ACTUAL COLUMN B TOTAL FOR LINE 2 IS /interestIncome, Form 1040 line 2b: half of every community item plus the whole of every separate item this taxpayer owns, which is exactly what "You must report half of all community income and all of your" separate income (line 124, LEFT column) describes. That identity holds on the population that can FILE; a return still carrying the spouse's separate item also carries that item whole on line 2b, which is column C's amount, and /interestReports/secondaryFilerUsedWithoutMFJ refuses that return.
THIS IS A HALF OF THE NET, NOT OF BOX 1, AND THE FORM 8958 READING IS STATED BECAUSE THE DISCLOSED FIGURE DEPENDS ON IT. The half is taken over ../taxableInterest PLUS ../taxableBondPremiumAndMarketDiscountAdjustment, i.e. over box 3 plus box 1 plus box 10 minus box 11 minus box 12 — the same per report quantity Form 1040 line 2b carries. Form 8958 line 2 says only "Identify the interest from each payer on separate lines. Enter the" total in column A (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f8958.pdf, page 4, LEFT column of a two column extraction); it does not say whether column A is the GROSS box 1 with the amortizable bond premium subtracted below, the way Schedule B presents it, or the NET. THIS DICTIONARY READS IT AS THE NET, and the reason is that the split must divide the amount that actually reaches the return: the alternative — halving box 1 and leaving the boxes 10 to 12 term whole — leaves the spouse's share of a bond premium or a market discount entirely on this return, which is a wrong DOLLAR rather than a presentation choice. The presentation residue this reading accepts is bounded, and BOTH of its numbers are stated because they differ by a factor of two and an earlier draft of this paragraph conflated them. Each of columns B and C is (box 1 + boxes 10 to 12)/2, so B + C = box 1 + boxes 10 to 12. If a filer transcribes column A as the GROSS box 1, the form's own footing rule misses by the WHOLE boxes 10 to 12 amount, while each column individually differs from half of gross by HALF of it. Reading column A as the NET, which is what this dictionary computes, makes B and C foot to A exactly, up to the one cent HALF EVEN residue disclosed above. The Schedule B presentation of the same quantity is unaffected — the ABP adjustment still sits below the line 1 payer list, where /interestIncome puts it.

Fact.Name: Form 8958 line 11 — the community half of this payer's box 4 that this unit moves
Fact.Description:
The taxpayer's allocated share of ONE Form 1099-INT's box 4 backup withholding, on the same items and the same halves as ../communityPropertyAllocatedInterestUnrounded, because the credit follows the income it was withheld from. $0 on every non community item and on every non allocation return — so, exactly as for the interest half above, this is the COMMUNITY HALF THIS UNIT MOVES and not the column B figure: column B of a separate property row is that row's whole box 4. The actual column B total for the Form 1099-INT leg of line 11 is taxCalculations:/form1099Withholding, Form 1040 line 25b. Cents preserved; Form 1040 line 25b rounds once at its own line.
THE READING, STATED BECAUSE THE HALF IS NOT PRINTED FOR THIS BOX. Form 8958 line 11 is a printed line covering withholding from ANY payer ("11 Taxes withheld", line 81; its instruction "Identify the taxes withheld from each payer or entity on separate", line 196 RIGHT column), and its instruction says to ALLOCATE without stating a ratio. The ratio one half comes from IRC 31(a)(1), which allows the credit to "the recipient of the income": where the item's income is split in half by state law, the credit on it follows in half. The form's own "Federal income tax withheld" paragraph states that conclusion explicitly for community WAGES only ("each of you is entitled to credit for half the income tax withheld on", line 182), which is why this fact carries the reasoning rather than a quote that covers it.

Fact.Name: Community-property allocated interest (Form 8958 line 2)
Fact.Description:
THE CONTRACT PATH. The COMMUNITY HALF of Form 8958 line 2 that this unit moves, totalled over every payer whose interest is community income, for the taxpayer whose return this is. Whole dollars: the per payer halves are summed WITH CENTS and the total is rounded once here.
IT IS NOT THE COLUMN B TOTAL, AND AN EARLIER VERSION OF THIS FACT SAID IT WAS [prose fix; the Derived body is unchanged and no number moves]. Form 8958 column A carries "Enter the total amount of your community or separate income," (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f8958.pdf, page 4, LEFT column of a two column extraction) and the columns must foot, "amounts in columns B and C. Together, columns B and C should" / "equal column A." (lines 201 and 202, LEFT column). So column B for this taxpayer is HALF THE COMMUNITY INCOME PLUS ALL OF THIS TAXPAYER'S OWN SEPARATE INCOME — which is the form's operative sentence read whole, "You must report half of all community income and all of your" separate income (line 124, LEFT column). This fact carries only the first of those two terms. On the mixed anchor return it is 1,200.00 while column B is 1,500.00, short by the taxpayer's own separate 300.00 item — a whole line item, not a rounding residue. THE ACTUAL COLUMN B TOTAL IS /interestIncome, Form 1040 line 2b, on the population that can file: it carries this half plus every separate item untouched. A return still holding the SPOUSE'S separate item carries that whole too, which is column C's amount, and /interestReports/secondaryFilerUsedWithoutMFJ refuses that return.
THE SPLIT RUNS BOTH WAYS on a community item — half the taxpayer's own interest leaves this return as well as half the spouse's arriving — and does NOT run at all on a separate property item, which is the whole difference from the wages row. So this total is NOT half of the collection: it is half of the COMMUNITY part of the collection, and the separate part reaches Form 1040 line 2b untouched.
This fact is the DISCLOSURE figure. The number Form 1040 line 2b actually carries moves through /communityPropertyInterestAllocationAdjustmentUnrounded.

Fact.Name: Community-property allocated interest withholding (Form 8958 line 11, interest leg)
Fact.Description:
The COMMUNITY HALF of Form 8958 line 11 that this unit moves, for Form 1099-INT box 4 only: half the backup withholding on the interest this return reports half of. Whole dollars, rounded once here over cents bearing addends.
NOT THE COLUMN B FIGURE, for the same reason as the interest total: column B also carries the whole box 4 of every SEPARATE property Form 1099-INT this taxpayer owns, which this fact reads $0 for. The actual column B total for this leg is taxCalculations:/form1099Withholding, Form 1040 line 25b.
IT IS A LEG, NOT THE LINE. Form 8958 line 11 covers every payer's withholding; this fact is the 1099-INT part of it, the dividend part is dividendReports:/communityPropertyAllocatedDividendWithholding, and the wage part is formW2s:/communityPropertyAllocatedFederalWithholding. The five other 1040 line 25b legs (SSA-1099, RRB-1099, 1099-G, 1099-MISC, 1099-R) are NOT allocated by this unit and are named as inherited gaps in interest_memory.json.

Fact.Name: The community interest half that leaves this return under Form 8958
Fact.Description:
A NEGATIVE, cents bearing addend: MINUS the sum of the per payer community halves.
WHY THE NEGATION AND NOT THE WAGES UNIT'S FORMULA, and this is the correction this unit had to make to the shape it inherited. formW2s:/communityPropertyWagesAllocationAdjustmentUnrounded is allocated MINUS unscoped, which is right only because EVERY W-2 is community income, so unscoped minus that adjustment collapses to the half. Here the collection is MIXED. Take a $1,000 community item and a $300 separate item of the taxpayer's own: the unscoped line 2b base is $1,300, the reportable figure is $500 plus $300 equals $800, and the wages formula would give 500 minus 1,300 equals minus 800, printing $500 — silently deleting the filer's OWN separate income from the line. The negation gives minus 500 and prints $800. It degenerates to the wages formula exactly when every item is community, which is why the wages row is correct as written.
WHY AN ADDEND AND NOT A REPLACEMENT: the footing discipline. /interestIncome computes Form 1040 line 2b through TWO arms (a Schedule B arm summing per payer ROUNDED amounts and a non Schedule B arm summing unrounded ones) and /requiresScheduleB tests a THIRD copy of the same base. One addend enters all three, so the printed line, the arm that prints it and the test that chooses the arm can never disagree about the allocation.
A BOUNDED RESIDUE IN THE SCHEDULE B ARM, disclosed rather than papered over: that arm sums amounts already rounded per payer and then takes this unrounded adjustment, so the two conventions mix and the arm can differ from a per payer rounded allocation by under a dollar per payer. A second, rounded basis adjustment was considered and rejected — it would put two different allocation figures in the dictionary for one Form 8958 line, which the footing discipline exists to prevent.
NO GATE ON THIS FACT, deliberately: every addend of the CollectionSum is already $0 whenever filers:/isCommunityPropertyAllocationReturn is false, so this fact is $0 there too, with one fewer gate read in front of Form 1040 line 2b. That gate is complete safe FALSE, so an unanswered domicile changes nothing.

Fact.Name: (Writable) Is this interest from a seller-financed mortgage on the buyer's personal residence?
Fact.Description: SCREEN: "Did you get this interest from a mortgage you financed yourself when you sold a home or other property?" Schedule B asks you to list this interest FIRST, ahead of your other payers, and to show the buyer's name, address, and Social Security number. You must also give the buyer your own SSN. If you do not show the buyer's name, address, and SSN, or do not give the buyer your SSN, you may have to pay a $50 penalty." (Instructions for Schedule B (Form 1040) (2025), Seller-financed mortgages, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sb.pdf, page 1.) ASKED WHEN: this interest report exists and the filer is entering it by hand rather than from a Form 1099-INT — seller-financed mortgage interest arrives with no Form 1099-INT, so the natural screen order is after ../has1099 is answered No; a Yes here on a report that also carries a Form 1099-INT is allowed, not blocked, because a buyer who files Form 1098 does issue one. UNANSWERED POSTURE: defaulted to No by ../isSellerFinancedMortgage, so no existing return changes and no filer is asked a question they have no reason to answer; the amount is on line 1 either way through ../taxableInterest, so nothing on Form 1040 turns on the default. VALIDATION: Boolean, Yes/No radio, no default selection. FEEDS: ../isSellerFinancedMortgage, which drives the buyer-identification questions below, the /sellerFinancedInterestReports ordering collection, and the Schedule B filing trigger for the seller-financed-mortgage bullet.

The IRS uses it to match your report of the interest against the mortgage-interest deduction the buyer claims. If the buyer does not have an SSN, enter the taxpayer identification number the buyer would use as the payer of mortgage interest on Form 1098. If you do not show the buyer's name, address, and SSN, you may have to pay a $50 penalty." (Instructions for Schedule B (Form 1040) (2025), Seller-financed mortgages, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sb.pdf, page 1.) ASKED WHEN: ../isSellerFinancedMortgage is true. Schedule B Part I line 1 has one payer/amount pair per row (dictionary/pdf/2025/IRS1040SB/en/configuration.yml); the buyer-identification text the instruction requires below the seller-financed entry has no PDF field mapped to it. This fact is drafted and asserted, not yet printed. If you do not show the buyer's name, address, and SSN, you may have to pay a $50 penalty." Enter that other person's share here. You must also give the actual owner a Form 1099-INT and file Forms 1096 and 1099-INT with the IRS, unless the owner is your spouse." (Instructions for Schedule B (Form 1040) (2025), Nominees, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sb.pdf, pages 1-2.) Report the whole box 1 amount on Schedule B line 1 and subtract what you paid the seller below the subtotal as Accrued Interest." (Instructions for Schedule B (Form 1040) (2025), Accrued interest, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sb.pdf, page 2; the payer side at https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1099int.pdf, page 3.) Fact.Name: U.S. Savings Bond Interest Previously Reported
Fact.Description: SCREEN: "Did you already report some of this savings bond interest on an earlier return? If so, how much of the amount in box 3 was reported in earlier years?" HELP TEXT: "If you chose to report your savings bond interest each year as it built up, instead of waiting until you cashed the bond, then the Form 1099-INT you get at redemption still shows the WHOLE accumulation in box 3 — the Treasury does not track your election. Report the whole box 3 amount on Schedule B line 1 and subtract the part you already reported below the subtotal as U.S. Savings Bond Interest Previously Reported. Pub. 550 Example 1: a $1,000 Series EE bond bought for $500.00 in March 2006 and redeemed in March 2025 for $913.60 has box 3 = $413.60, of which only $7.20 accrued in 2025; you subtract $406.40." (Pub. 550 (2025), Interest Income, Example 1, sources/p550-ty2025-2026-07.xml lines 1371-1373.) ASKED WHEN: this report carries a Form 1099-INT box 3 amount and the filer has said they elected annual accrual on savings bond interest. UNANSWERED POSTURE: defaulted to $0 by ../savingsBondInterestPreviouslyReported. That default is the pre-election posture — a filer who never elected annual accrual reports the whole redemption increase, which is the correct answer for the great majority — and it is why the question must be ASKED of any filer with box 3, not merely offered. VALIDATION: Dollar, Min $0; entered positive, subtracted. FEEDS: ../scheduleBLine1Adjustment.

Section 454(c) includes the redemption increase only "to the extent not previously includible in gross income", but Treasury does not track the election, so box 3 at redemption shows the entire accumulation. Schedule B subtracts this below the line-1 subtotal under the label "U.S. Savings Bond Interest Previously Reported". Complete-safe $0.

Schedule B has ONE mechanic for every case in which box 1 or box 3 overstates the filer's own income — report the payer's whole figure on line 1, write a named label under the last entry, subtract, and put the result on line 2 — and these three are three labels of that one mechanic. It is the same shape and the same placement as ../taxableBondPremiumAndMarketDiscountAdjustment, which carries the fourth label, "ABP Adjustment". Fact.Description: The taxable leg of the boxes 10 to 13 net: the rollup less the tax-exempt leg it contains, which leaves exactly box 10 minus box 11 minus box 12. Written as that subtraction rather than as a second sum of the same three boxes so the rollup is the one place the four box terms are combined. Carries its own sign, so /interestIncome adds a single term. Applied at the Form 1040 line 2b TOTAL rather than netted into each payer's Schedule B Part I line 1 entry. For boxes 11 and 12 that is what Schedule B says to do: subtract the premium below the line-1 list, identified as "ABP Adjustment". For box 10 it is not - the instruction puts accrued market discount on line 1 itself - and the box-10 term is carried at the total anyway; the authority comment states the sourced reason the line-2b number is the same, and states the bounded rounding and MeF-presentation residue that reason does not cover.

Fact.Description:
The signed box 10 less box 11 less box 12 net, summed over every interest report on the return: the single term /interestIncome already adds in BOTH arms of its Schedule B switch, given a name of its own. It is named because it is a RETURN-LEVEL term of Form 1040 line 2b that /primaryFilerInterestTotal and /secondaryFilerInterestTotal deliberately leave out - each of those Descriptions says the boxes 10 to 12 adjustment is not divided between the filers - so a consumer that needs ONE filer's own line 2b cannot tell whether it is looking at the whole of that filer's interest unless it can also see whether this residue is present. Nothing about how the adjustment is computed changes here; the per-report fact it sums, /interestReports/*/taxableBondPremiumAndMarketDiscountAdjustment, carries the boxes, the signs and the Schedule B placement reasoning.
COMPLETE-SAFE $0 ON A RETURN THAT NEVER OPENED THE INTEREST SECTION. An answered but EMPTY collection takes the first arm and sums to $0.
TYPE/SIGN/ROUNDING: Dollar, integer cents, SIGNED - box 10 adds and boxes 11 and 12 subtract, so this total is negative on a return whose premium exceeds its market discount. No rounding here; /interestIncome rounds where it is assembled.

Fact.Name: Knockout Has Bonds - NARROWED THREE TIMES; since 2026-08-21 it is the box-8-not-established completeness gate and nothing else
Fact.Description:
Whether the filer is knocked out for holding bonds. IT FIRES ON ONE THING ONLY: the sum, across every interest report, of the box-9 specified private activity bond interest carried on a report whose BOX 8 IS NOT ESTABLISHED, greater than $0. Box 8 is unestablished exactly when the report's ../has1099 discriminator is unanswered, so this is a pure DATA-COMPLETENESS refusal and nothing else.
WHAT THE GATE IS. Box 9 nests INSIDE box 8 by the payer instruction - "Include specified private activity bond interest in box 9 and in the total for box 8" (2025 Instructions for Form 1099-INT, "Box 8. Tax-Exempt Interest", https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1099int.pdf, page 3) - so a box 9 with a box 8 that covers it is the CORRECTLY-PREPARED form, and a box 9 larger than its box 8 is a form no payer can issue. This fact distinguishes them, per report, on the same shape this repo already established for an amount entered without its base (formW2s:/hasOasdiWithholdingWithoutOasdiWages): the inconsistency is the refusal, not the amount. Boxes 10 through 13 are outside this gate - they are computed on /interestReports/*/bondPremiumAndMarketDiscountAdjustment and its two signed legs, wired to Form 1040 line 2a and 2b directly - and the gate does not reach Form 1099-DIV box-13 fund holders, who have no box 9.
THE THREE CELLS A NONZERO BOX 9 ARRIVES IN, and why the box-9 term is a per-report gate rather than a term the CollectionSum keeps whole. (a) BOX 9 WITH A BOX 8 THAT COVERS IT - the well-formed Form 1099-INT - FILES: Form 1040 line 2a carries the box-8 total, which by the payer instruction already INCLUDES box 9; the IRC 57(a)(5) preference computes on both legs (form6251:/amtLine2gPrivateActivityBondInterest); and the IRC 163(d) widening (form6251:/amtLine2cInvestmentInterestDelta) is ordered before it. At the boundary, box 8 = box 9 the floor on /interestReports/*/taxExemptInterest is inert and line 2a keeps box 8; one cent below it the floor is active and line 2a becomes box 9.
(b) BOX 9 WITH BOX 8 AT $0 OR BLANK - FILES. /interestReports/*/taxExemptInterest floors box 8 at its own report's box 9, so Form 1040 line 2a reads the box-9 amount rather than a figure the graph knows is short. (c) BOX 9 WITH THE REPORT'S ../has1099 DISCRIMINATOR UNANSWERED is the one cell this fact still refuses. /interestReports/*/taxExemptInterest is Incomplete there by its own deliberate design, so /taxExemptInterest is Incomplete regardless of what this fact says; the refusal is a pure data-completeness backstop, not a computed protection. THE GATE IS PER REPORT, measured rather than assumed: the Switch nests directly inside the CollectionSum's Add, so each arm's box-8 and box-9 dependencies bind to the SAME collection item; a gate that instead read a collection-level box-8 total against each report's box 9 would free returns it must refuse. THE COMPLETENESS ARM is where that shape stops transferring whole: it compares DERIVED complete-safe box facts because for a W-2 "a missing wage box IS the defect" (formW2s box 3 defaults to a complete $0), but Form 1099-INT box 8 does NOT. /interestReports/*/taxExemptInterest resolves THREE ways - Complete (../has1099 answered), INCOMPLETE (a box-8 amount with ../has1099 unanswered, the "amount present, discriminator unanswered" cell), and PLACEHOLDER $0 (no box-8 amount with ../has1099 unanswered) - and a bare comparison against the last two would carry that incompleteness into a knockout and from there into flow:/flowIsKnockedOut. So the body tests Not(IsComplete(box 8)) FIRST and contributes the box-9 amount there, before the comparison is reached: an unestablished box 8 cannot be shown to cover box 9, so cell (c) stays REFUSED at nil cost - its return cannot resolve either way. Both completeness states are witnessed separately.
SO THE REFUSAL IS EXACTLY THE UNESTABLISHED BOX 8. Cell (c) is refused; cells (a) and (b) file.
THE AMT COUPLING IS LIVE: form6251:/knockoutAmtUnmodeledPreference reads that a box-9 amount can carry a five-year-property rental filer over the AMT exemption at arm 2, on the same return that /flowKnockoutHasBonds no longer refuses at cell (a). MEASURED both ways on one base return - with a single well-formed Form 1099-INT added: at box 8 = box 9 = $500,000 this fact goes false while /knockoutAmtUnmodeledPreference goes TRUE and the return is refused for a stated reason; at box 8 = box 9 = $1,000 both are false and the filer FILES.
TAX-EXEMPT OID IS OUTSIDE THIS GATE. It routes to line 2a from Form 1099-OID box 2 (when the report classifies it tax-exempt) and box 11, and it has an intake: /taxExemptInterest sums it through /taxExemptOriginalIssueDiscountTotal, and a Form 1099-OID record missing its own box 2 amount, tax-exempt classification or box 11 amount blocks through /hasIncompleteOriginalIssueDiscountReports. This fact reads Form 1099-INT box 9 alone, so no Form 1099-OID amount is a reason to keep or to widen it.
ONE RESIDUE IS UNREACHABLE BY INPUT and is named so it is not mistaken for a reason to keep this refusal: the section 265 disallowed-expense family behind the IRC 57(a)(5)(A) reduction has no intake; form4952:/investmentExpenses is the REGULAR-tax allowable investment expense, a different thing. A refusal has to be reachable to protect anyone.
WIRING: refusal by MEMBERSHIP, not by an own tag. This fact carries Export downstreamFacts and NO BlockSubmissionOnTrue; it blocks by being a member of flow:/flowIsKnockedOut, which carries the tag, and it is also a member of imported:/knockoutInterestIncome, a post-import aggregate with no submission tag at all. A future edit must not "restore" a BlockSubmissionOnTrue this fact has never had.

Fact.Name: Schedule B line 4: total taxable interest after the series EE and I exclusion and the line-1 adjustments
Fact.Description:
The printed Schedule B line 4 amount - line 2 (the sum of every line 1 payer entry and every other taxable interest term this dictionary carries) less line 3 (the series EE and I savings bond exclusion from Form 8815) and less the below-the-subtotal line-1 adjustments - rounded once at the total. It is the figure the form sends to Form 1040 line 2b, and it is the figure BOTH of the schedule's over-$1,500 tests read.
NOT NEW ARITHMETIC. Every term and the single Round were already inline inside /requiresScheduleB, exactly as they stand here; this fact gives them a name so that /requiresScheduleB (whether to USE the schedule) and /requiresScheduleBPartIII (whether to COMPLETE Part III) test the same total. Two inline copies of a nine-term sum is the drift this module's own discipline exists to prevent, and the two tests are on DIFFERENT sides of the Form 8815 subtraction only because the form puts them there.
THE ROUNDING IS PART OF THE PRINTED TEST: the instruction tests "the total", and a return that rounds must round all amounts, so an unrounded 1,500.01 prints 1,500 on line 2b and is not over the threshold. Rounding once at the total, not per term, is what reproduces the printed line.
NOT the same as /interestIncome, which is a Switch whose other arm is the no-Schedule-B route; this fact is the Schedule B arm's own total and carries no route decision.

Fact.Name: Schedule B Part III must be completed (a condition distinct from using Schedule B at all)
Fact.Description:
TRUE when the filer must complete Schedule B Part III, Foreign Accounts and Trusts. The Part III header states its own three conditions: over $1,500 of taxable interest or ordinary dividends, a foreign account, or a distribution from - or being a grantor of or transferor to - a foreign trust. The form repeats the first of them twice more, as the note under line 4 and the note under line 6.
WHY THIS IS NOT /requiresScheduleB, which is the point of the fact. The General Instructions list decides whether to USE Schedule B and has eight entries, most of them with no dollar threshold at all: a $1 nominee distribution, a seller-financed mortgage, any amortizable bond premium. Part III has three. So the two conditions genuinely differ, and the difference is reachable in both directions on ordinary returns: an amortizable-bond-premium filer reporting $400 of interest must use Schedule B and must NOT complete Part III, and so must a filer whose $700 of interest drops to $500 after the series EE and I exclusion. Before this fact the graph held one Boolean for both jobs, so every such filer was carried to Part III.
THE INTEREST SIDE IS TESTED ON LINE 4 AND NOT ON LINE 2. The note that states this condition sits directly under line 4, AFTER the Form 8815 subtraction, while the use-Schedule-B trigger reads the same total for a different purpose. The dividends side is line 6, which is income:/ordinaryDividends, the same fact /requiresScheduleB reads.
COMPLETE SAFETY comes from the same places /requiresScheduleB gets it: /scheduleBLine4TotalTaxableInterest is complete-safe over a listed interest collection, income:/ordinaryDividends carries its own complete-safe 0, and income:/hasForeignAccountsOrTrusts is the fact the eighth General Instructions bullet already reads. Witness per-filer-total-no-reports-complete-safe for the no-reports arm.
NO CONSUMER YET, which is why it carries an Export. Schedule B has no render gate in dictionary/pdf/2025, so nothing in this dictionary prints Part III conditionally today; when a Schedule B print gate is built this is the fact that decides whether Part III prints, and the application is what stops asking lines 7a, 7b and 8 of a filer who does not have to answer them.

Fact.Name: Federal income tax withheld (box 4), cents preserved
Fact.Description:
Box 4 of Form 1099-INT, federal income tax withheld, AS REPORTED — cents preserved, not rounded. Complete-safe (0 when there is no 1099-INT, and 0 when the writable is left unanswered): the nested Switch is the one /interestReports/*/taxWithheld carries, moved here unchanged.
WHY THIS EXISTS: the line-25b leg. This is the ADDEND fact — what taxCalculations:/form1099Withholding (Form 1040 line 25b) sums. i1040gi routes 1099 interest withholding to that line in as many words ("If you received a 2025 Form 1099 showing federal income tax withheld on dividends, taxable or tax-exempt interest income ... include the amount withheld in the total on line 25b"), and line 25b adds two or more amounts, so i1040gi page 23 governs it in full: "include cents when adding the amounts and round off only the total". Summing already-rounded per-document box 4s is what that sentence forbids. Form 1040 line 25b already carries its own single Round, so the term does its job by handing the cents upward and rounding nothing itself.
DO NOT use this fact as a stand-in for box 4 on a printed line or in an export — it deliberately carries cents. The per-document whole-dollar image is /interestReports/*/taxWithheld, which is now this fact wrapped in Round and did NOT move.
WHY THE SIBLING SHAPE, and not the in-place unwrap the 1099-R term took. Taking the Round off /interestReports/*/taxWithheld would have been a FLOW change, not a rounding change. Three readers depend on its whole-dollar image: /interestReports/*/isComplete tests it for equality with 0 to decide whether a payer TIN is required, /interestReports/*/hasFederalWithholding gates that same TIN question on it being greater than 0, and it is Export mef="true", standing for one document's printed box. A box 4 of 0.40 rounds to 0 today; unwrapped it would stop doing so and the return would begin demanding a payer TIN it does not need. form1099Rs could unwrap in place precisely because its MeF surface is a SEPARATE fact (/form1099Rs/*/federalWithholdingExport) and nothing read its rounded image. Here the item fact IS the MeF surface, which is the /formW2s/*/federalWithholdingUnrounded case exactly.

THAT WAS NOT COSMETIC RESTRAINT. This is the /formW2s/*/federalWithholding shape, not the /form1099Rs/*/federalWithholding one, because there the MeF surface is a separate fact and here it is this one. See /interestReports/*/taxWithheldUnrounded for the full derivation.

Fact.Name: Knockout Has Foreign Tax Paid - NARROWED 2026-08-17 to a box-6/no-1116-intake consistency gate
Fact.Description:
Fires when some Form 1099-INT reports a nonzero box 6 (foreign tax paid) AND the no-Form-1116 foreign tax credit intake (foreignTaxCredit:/writableForeignTaxPaid) does not cover that box-6 total - i.e. the intake is unanswered, or it is answered at less than the sum of box 6 across the filer's interest reports.
WHAT THIS FACT USED TO BE, AND WHY THAT STOPPED BEING RIGHT. The body was Count(box 6 != $0) > 0: any nonzero box 6 anywhere refused the whole return. That was correct when it was inherited, because this dictionary had no foreign tax credit at all. The dictionary now ships one - foreignTaxCredit:/foreignTaxCreditAmount, the Schedule 3 line 1 no-Form-1116 exception, with the $300/$600 threshold enforced and the smaller-of line-16 cap modeled - and nobody came back to this guard. So the module that made the refusal unnecessary for the ordinary small-investor case has been shipping while the refusal kept turning that same filer away: a fill that lands in one module and stops there, leaving a stale guard standing in another.
THE POPULATION FREED is exactly the filer the printed Exception is written for - foreign tax withheld on 1099-INT interest, at or under $300 ($600 MFJ), who today is refused outright and after this narrowing files with the credit on Schedule 3 line 1.
WHY A CONSISTENCY GATE RATHER THAN A RETIREMENT, and this is the whole design. The credit is computed from a SEPARATE scalar intake (foreignTaxCredit:/writableForeignTaxPaid, the total foreign tax across 1099-INT box 6, 1099-DIV box 7 and Schedule K-3), not from box 6. Retiring this guard outright would let a filer who reported box 6 and never answered that scalar file a return with a $0 foreign tax credit and no surfacing - a silent DENIAL of a credit the filer is owed, which is the exact World-#1 failure mode foreignTaxCredit:/knockoutForeignTaxRequiresForm1116 was created for. So the refusal is kept precisely where the two intakes disagree, which is the shape this repo already uses twice: formW2s:/hasOasdiWithholdingWithoutOasdiWages (an amount entered without its base) and this module's own /flowKnockoutHasBonds box-8/box-9 gate. The inconsistency is the refusal, not the amount.
GREATER-THAN-OR-EQUAL, NOT EQUAL, and the asymmetry is deliberate. Only the BELOW direction is this gate's business: a scalar below the box-6 sum means the return is claiming less foreign tax than its own attached forms report, which is the under-credit this gate exists to catch. The slack ABOVE the sum is licensed by what the graph already does; the reasoning below is what adversarial review corrected it to, because the first wording rested on the wrong thing.
THE LOAD-BEARING REASON: /writableForeignTaxPaid is an unguarded taxpayer-attested writable for EVERY filer without box 6. Nothing in this dictionary checks it against any reported form, and a filer with no 1099-INT at all can answer it at any figure up to the threshold and be credited. So permitting a scalar above the box-6 sum creates NO new over-statement surface - it stops box-6 filers being the one population accidentally protected from that surface by an unrelated refusal. It does mean a filer who reports $250 of box 6 and answers the scalar $290 now files with $290 credited, $40 of it unsupported by anything on the return, where the old blanket body refused them. That direction is stated rather than left silent, and it is a pre-existing property of the scalar rather than one this gate introduces. Policing scalar inflation is foreignTaxCredit's own question (its MED row, and the printed Exception's conditions 1 and 3), not a 1099-INT box's.
WHAT IS ONLY CONTEXT, and was wrongly written as the reason until the review: the scalar is the TOTAL across 1099-INT box 6, 1099-DIV box 7 and Schedule K-3, so requiring EQUALITY would in principle refuse a dividend-holding filer for being correct. That is true of the printed instruction and FALSE OF THIS TREE TODAY - neither 1099-DIV box 7 nor Schedule K-3 has any fact in dictionary/ty2025/, so no fact could substantiate a dollar of the slack. The direction is right for the graph we will have; the paragraph above is why it is safe in the graph we have.
THE OVER-THRESHOLD CASE IS NOT WEAKENED - IT IS HANDED OVER. A box-6 filer whose covering scalar exceeds $300/$600 passes THIS gate and is then refused by foreignTaxCredit:/knockoutForeignTaxRequiresForm1116, which is the knockout that actually names Form 1116 and carries its own BlockSubmissionOnTrue. No return that was refused for being above the threshold becomes filable here.
ONE CELL OF THAT HAND-OFF IS INCOMPLETE RATHER THAN TRUE, found on adversarial review and recorded rather than papered over. /knockoutForeignTaxRequiresForm1116 compares against foreignTaxCredit:/foreignTaxNoForm1116Threshold, a Switch on filingStatus:/isFilingStatusMFJ with NO unanswered arm - so with filing status unanswered the threshold is Incomplete, the GreaterThan is Incomplete, and that knockout is Incomplete rather than true. The old blanket body here refused such a return Complete true regardless of filing status, so this IS a behaviour change and it is named. IT IS UNREACHABLE: a return with no filing status is not filable on other grounds, and flow:/flowIsKnockedOut is an Any that cannot go true off an Incomplete member either way, so no filer's outcome differs. THE CONSERVATIVE FIX - default the threshold to the $300 arm when filing status is unanswered - IS NOT MADE HERE because it is an edit to foreignTaxCredit.xml; making it from this module would be exactly the boundary crossing this fill declined everywhere else. Routed, not fixed.
WHAT THIS NARROWING DOES NOT DO, named so it is not read as more than it is. It does not derive the credit from box 6 - the scalar remains the sole input to foreignTaxCredit:/foreignTaxCreditAmount and this fact edits no other module. It does not touch the Exception's conditions 1 and 3 (all foreign source gross income reported on 1099-INT/1099-DIV/K-3; the 16-day holding rule), which remain unrepresented in the graph - this gate makes that gap REACHABLE for the box-6 filer, where before the refusal hid it, and that widening is stated rather than left silent. It does not reach Form 1099-DIV box 7, which has no fact anywhere in dictionary/ty2025/ (dividendReports.xml contains no foreign-tax field at all), so the dividend half of the same intake is a NAMED GAP this unit does not close.
WIRING: refusal by MEMBERSHIP, not by an own tag - Export downstreamFacts and no BlockSubmissionOnTrue, blocking through flow:/flowIsKnockedOut, exactly as before. A future edit must not "restore" a BlockSubmissionOnTrue this fact has never had.
ADDITIVE ON THE COMMITTED CORPUS: the only committed box-6 answer is $0.00 (scenarios/upstream/mfs-4300-none.json), so the first conjunct is false on every committed scenario and this fact resolves Complete false everywhere it did before.
