Fact.Name: Taxable interest attributed to this filer
Fact.Description: One filer's own taxable interest: Form 1099-INT box 1 plus Form 1099-INT box 3 plus interest received with no Form 1099-INT, added up over the interest reports attributed to that filer. Box 3 is a separate aggregate from box 1 on the payee statement and both belong here. Tax-exempt interest (box 8) is excluded because it is not taxable interest, and the return-level terms Form 1040 line 2b also carries - the boxes 10 to 12 bond premium and market discount adjustment, the Form 8815 exclusion, the Form 8958 community-property allocation and the Schedule K-1 interest - are not divided between the filers here, so the two filers' figures do not add up to line 2b. The Schedule B line-1 below-the-subtotal subtractions (the nominee distribution, the accrued interest paid to a bond seller, and the savings bond interest already reported in earlier years) are also not divided between the filers here, though for a different reason: each is a per-payer amount, but Schedule B subtracts all three only ONCE, below the printed per-payer line-1 list, never against one payer's own entry - the same reason /interestReports/*/taxableInterest, the per-report fact this total is the per-filer counterpart of, keeps them out too.

Fact.Name: Form 8958 line 2 column A, this payer's total interest
Fact.Description: The total interest from ONE payer that Form 8958 line 2 column A prints: the taxable interest of the report plus its Form 1099-INT boxes 10 to 12 leg, signed. That is exactly the per report quantity Form 1040 line 2b carries and exactly the quantity the shipping half /interestReports/*/communityPropertyAllocatedInterestUnrounded is a half of, so columns B and C foot to this column. Not rounded: the halves are cent scale, and the form's footing rule is a cent rule, not a dollar rule. No shipping fact holds this sum; /interestReports/*/taxableInterest alone would drop the premium and market discount leg and the column would not foot.

Fact.Name: Form 8958 line 2 column B, this return's share of this payer's interest
Fact.Description: The share of ONE payer's interest that belongs on THIS separate return, which Form 8958 line 2 column B prints. On an allocated community row it is the community half the shipping fact already computes; on every other row it is the whole item, because a separate property item that reaches a filable separate return is this taxpayer's own (interest:/interestReports/secondaryFilerUsedWithoutMFJ blocks submission otherwise). The register prints this return's taxpayer in column B and the spouse or RDP in column C, matching the order of the page 1 identity block. Off gate the whole item is this return's, which is the ordinary separate return answer.

Fact.Name: Form 8958 line 2 column C, the other spouse or RDP share of this payer's interest
Fact.Description: The share of ONE payer's interest that belongs to the other spouse or RDP, which Form 8958 line 2 column C prints. It is column A minus column B by construction, which is how the form's own instruction "Together, columns B and C should equal column A" is made to hold exactly. On an odd cent community row the shipping half rounds to the even cent and column B takes it, so the residual cent lands here rather than breaking the footing; that is a disclosed consequence of a per payer allocation printed in cents. $0 on a separate property row, where column A and column B are both the whole item.

Fact.Name: Form 8958 line 2 row is an allocated community income row
Fact.Description: True when this Form 1099-INT sits on a return that must allocate community income AND the filer has characterised this payer's interest as community income. It is the condition the shipping fact /interestReports/*/communityPropertyAllocatedInterestUnrounded already switches on, lifted to a fact of its own so the Form 8958 line 2 column B and column C facts can select on the same test rather than restating it. False on an ordinary return and false on a separate property row, which is why silence about the character of an item never allocates it.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-INT calendar year
Fact.Description: The "For calendar year" entry printed in the form's title block, as a four-digit year. SCREEN SPEC: ask "Calendar year shown on this Form 1099-INT" (four digits), on the payer-identity screen, on every interest report; never required. Help text: the year the payer printed after "For calendar year" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f1099int.pdf, page 2); a form for a year other than 2025 belongs on that year's return or is a corrected prior-year form. Validation: exactly four digits. UNANSWERED: complete-safe; ../isComplete does not read it. WHAT IT FEEDS: nothing federal. Stored for the state and local returns and printed on the Form 1099-INT register.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-INT VOID box
Fact.Description: The VOID checkbox in the form's header. It prints on Copy A and Copy 1 only (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f1099int.pdf, pages 2-3); the recipient's Copy B and Copy 2 carry CORRECTED alone. SCREEN SPEC: ask "Is the VOID box checked on this Form 1099-INT?" (yes/no), on every interest report; never required. Help text: a payer checks VOID only on a Copy A it did not mean to file, so the IRS scanner skips it; a correction is never marked VOID. Validation: Boolean. UNANSWERED: complete-safe; ../isComplete does not read it. WHAT IT FEEDS: nothing federal. Stored for the state and local returns and printed on the Form 1099-INT register.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-INT CORRECTED box
Fact.Description: The CORRECTED checkbox in the form's header. It prints on every copy: beside VOID on Copy A and Copy 1 (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f1099int.pdf, pages 2-3) and as "CORRECTED (if checked)" alone on Copy B and Copy 2 (lines 93 and 173). SCREEN SPEC: ask "Is the CORRECTED box checked on this Form 1099-INT?" (yes/no), on every interest report; never required. Help text: a checked CORRECTED means this form replaces one the payer already sent; enter the corrected figures, not both forms. Validation: Boolean. UNANSWERED: complete-safe; ../isComplete does not read it. WHAT IT FEEDS: nothing federal. Stored for the state and local returns and printed on the Form 1099-INT register.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-INT payer's RTN
Fact.Description: The "Payer's RTN (optional)" box in the form's top right block, as printed (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f1099int.pdf, page 2). SCREEN SPEC: ask "Payer's RTN, if the form shows one" (free text), on the payer-identity screen, on every interest report; never required. Help text: the payer instruction makes this box optional -- a financial institution taking part in the direct-deposit-of-refunds program may enter its routing transit number (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1099int.pdf, page 2, RIGHT column); most forms leave it blank. Validation: free text. UNANSWERED: complete-safe; ../isComplete does not read it. WHAT IT FEEDS: nothing federal. Stored for the state and local returns and printed on the Form 1099-INT register.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-INT recipient's name
Fact.Description: The RECIPIENT'S name box, as printed (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f1099int.pdf, page 2). SCREEN SPEC: ask "Recipient's name as shown on this Form 1099-INT" (free text), on the recipient screen after ../filer, on every interest report; never required. Help text: copy the name the payer printed, even when it differs from the name on this return (a trust name, a maiden name); which person on the return received the form is ../filer, not this box. Validation: free text. UNANSWERED: complete-safe; ../isComplete does not read it. WHAT IT FEEDS: nothing federal. Stored for the state and local returns and printed on the Form 1099-INT register.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-INT recipient's street address
Fact.Description: The "Street address (including apt. no.)" box of the recipient block, as printed (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f1099int.pdf, page 2). SCREEN SPEC: ask "Recipient's street address as shown on this Form 1099-INT" (free text), on the recipient screen beneath the recipient's name, on every interest report; never required. Help text: copy the address the payer printed even when the return's own address has since changed; the return's mailing address is /address, not this box. Validation: free text. UNANSWERED: complete-safe; ../isComplete does not read it. WHAT IT FEEDS: nothing federal. Stored for the state and local returns and printed on the Form 1099-INT register.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-INT recipient's city, state and ZIP
Fact.Description: The "City or town, state or province, country, and ZIP or foreign postal code" box of the recipient block, as printed (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f1099int.pdf, page 2). SCREEN SPEC: ask "Recipient's city, state and ZIP as shown on this Form 1099-INT" (free text), on the recipient screen beneath the street address, on every interest report; never required. Help text: one line, exactly as the payer printed it, foreign postal codes included. Validation: free text. UNANSWERED: complete-safe; ../isComplete does not read it. WHAT IT FEEDS: nothing federal. Stored for the state and local returns and printed on the Form 1099-INT register.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-INT account number
Fact.Description: The "Account number (see instructions)" box, as printed (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f1099int.pdf, page 2). SCREEN SPEC: ask "Account number shown on this Form 1099-INT" (free text), on the payer-identity screen, on every interest report; never required. Help text: the payer instruction makes the account number required only where the payer files more than one Form 1099-INT for the same recipient (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1099int.pdf, page 2, RIGHT column), so many forms leave it blank; it is the payer's own account reference, not a bank routing number. Validation: free text. UNANSWERED: complete-safe; ../isComplete does not read it. WHAT IT FEEDS: nothing federal. Stored for the state and local returns and printed on the Form 1099-INT register.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-INT 2nd TIN not. box
Fact.Description: The "2nd TIN not." checkbox, as printed on Copy A (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f1099int.pdf, page 2). SCREEN SPEC: ask "Is the '2nd TIN not.' box checked on this Form 1099-INT?" (yes/no), on the payer-identity screen, on every interest report; never required. Help text: the payer enters an "X" here after the IRS has told it twice within three calendar years that the payee gave an incorrect TIN (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1099int.pdf, page 2, RIGHT column); it prints on the payer's Copy A, so a recipient copy usually shows nothing. Validation: Boolean. UNANSWERED: complete-safe; ../isComplete does not read it. WHAT IT FEEDS: nothing federal. Stored for the state and local returns and printed on the Form 1099-INT register.

Fact.Name: Investment expenses, Form 1099-INT box 5
Fact.Description: Form 1099-INT box 5, as printed (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f1099int.pdf, page 2). SCREEN SPEC: ask "Box 5, investment expenses" (dollars), on the interest-boxes screen, on every interest report; never required. Help text: box 5 is filled only by a single-class REMIC, and it shows the recipient's share of the REMIC's investment expenses (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1099int.pdf, page 3, RIGHT column); a bank's Form 1099-INT leaves it blank. Validation: not negative. UNANSWERED: complete-safe; ../isComplete does not read it. WHAT IT FEEDS: nothing federal -- the miscellaneous itemized deduction this box once fed is suspended for TY2025 by IRC 67(g), so no federal line reads it. Stored for the state and local returns (a state that decouples from 67(g) reads it by module-qualified path) and printed on the Form 1099-INT register.

Fact.Name: Foreign country or U.S. territory, Form 1099-INT box 7
Fact.Description: Form 1099-INT box 7, as printed (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f1099int.pdf, page 2): the NAME of the foreign country or U.S. territory the box 6 foreign tax was paid to. SCREEN SPEC: ask "Box 7, foreign country or U.S. territory" (free text), on the interest-boxes screen beside box 6, on every interest report; never required. Help text: the payer enters the name of the country or territory for which the box 6 tax was withheld (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1099int.pdf, page 3, RIGHT column); leave it blank when box 6 is blank. Validation: free text. UNANSWERED: complete-safe; ../isComplete does not read it. WHAT IT FEEDS: nothing federal. The box 6 AMOUNT is modeled by ../writableForeignTaxPaid and keeps its own consumers; this box is the country NAME beside it, and the Form 1116 country selection is its own separate intake in form1116.xml. Stored for the state and local returns and printed on the Form 1099-INT register.

Fact.Name: Payer's state, Form 1099-INT box 15, second state row
Fact.Description: Form 1099-INT box 15 as the payer prints it in the SECOND state row: the two-letter abbreviation of a state, one of the fifty states or the District of Columbia (constants:/statesAndDistrictsOptions). The printed form carries two state rows separated by a dash line -- "Use the state information boxes to report payments for up to two states. Keep the information for each state separated by the dash line." (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1099int.pdf, page 4, LEFT column) -- and this is the printed multiplicity. The FIRST row is ../writablePayerStateAbbreviation, unchanged. SCREEN SPEC: ask "Box 15, state (second row)" (a state or DC), on the state-rows screen beneath the first row, on every interest report; never required. Help text: only a form that shows two state rows fills this; leave it blank otherwise. Validation: one of /statesAndDistrictsOptions. UNANSWERED: complete-safe; ../isComplete does not read it. WHAT IT FEEDS: nothing federal -- box 15 is a state key and the federal return has no use for which state a payer withheld for. NOT THE SAME FACT as ../writableState, which is a two-member sameState/differentState enum and is kept unchanged. Stored for the state and local returns and printed on the Form 1099-INT register.

Fact.Name: State identification number, Form 1099-INT box 16, second state row
Fact.Description: Form 1099-INT box 16 in the SECOND state row: the payer's state identification number for the second state. The printed form carries two state rows separated by a dash line (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1099int.pdf, page 4, LEFT column), and this is the printed multiplicity; the FIRST row is ../writableStateIdNumber, unchanged. SCREEN SPEC: ask "Box 16, state identification number (second row)" (free text), on the state-rows screen beside the second-row state, on every interest report; never required. Help text: the payer's number assigned by that second state; leave it blank when the form shows one state row. Validation: free text. UNANSWERED: complete-safe; ../isComplete does not read it. WHAT IT FEEDS: nothing federal. Stored for the state and local returns and printed on the Form 1099-INT register.

Fact.Name: State tax withheld, Form 1099-INT box 17, second state row
Fact.Description: Form 1099-INT box 17 in the SECOND state row: the state income tax the payer withheld for the second state. The printed form carries two state rows separated by a dash line (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1099int.pdf, page 4, LEFT column), and this is the printed multiplicity; the FIRST row is ../writableStateTaxWithheld, unchanged. SCREEN SPEC: ask "Box 17, state tax withheld (second row)" (dollars), on the state-rows screen beside the second-row state identification number, on every interest report; never required. Help text: only a form that shows two state rows fills this. Validation: not negative. UNANSWERED: complete-safe; ../isComplete does not read it. WHAT IT FEEDS: nothing federal, and deliberately nothing here either. The first row's ../stateTaxWithheld rolls up into /stateAndLocalIncomeTaxWithheldFromInterest, which that fact's own Description records as a DISCLOSURE no consumer reads; adding a second row to that roll-up would change a shipping total, so it is a drafted successor, not part of this intake unit. Stored for the state and local returns and printed on the Form 1099-INT register.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-OID reports
Fact.Description: Per-payer Form 1099-OID reports. The tax-exempt legs -- box 2 stated interest when the obligation is tax-exempt, and box 11 tax-exempt OID, each net of the box 6 and box 10 premiums -- reach Form 1040 line 2a. The taxable legs -- box 1, box 8 and box 2 when the obligation is taxable, adjusted by boxes 5, 6 and 10 -- reach Form 1040 line 2b as Schedule B Part I line 1 entries. Box 4 reaches Form 1040 line 25b and box 3 reaches Schedule 1 line 18.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-OID box 2 stated interest
Fact.Description: SCREEN. Enter the qualified stated interest reported in box 2; a blank box may be left blank (it reads $0).

Fact.Name: Form 1099-OID box 2 is tax-exempt interest
Fact.Description: SCREEN. When box 11 is $0, is the qualified stated interest in box 2 tax-exempt? If box 11 is positive, Form 1099-OID instructions classify box 2 as tax-exempt automatically.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-OID box 11 tax-exempt OID
Fact.Description: SCREEN. Enter the tax-exempt original issue discount reported in box 11; a blank box may be left blank (it reads $0).

Fact.Name: Form 1099-OID box 2 stated interest, $0 when blank
Fact.Description: Box 2 as entered, floored at $0, or $0 when the box is not answered: a payer leaves box 2 blank on an obligation with no qualified stated interest. Every box 2 leg reads this, never the writable.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-OID box 11 tax-exempt OID, $0 when blank
Fact.Description: Box 11 as entered, floored at $0, or $0 when the box is not answered: a payer leaves box 11 blank on a taxable obligation. Every box 11 leg reads this, never the writable.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-OID obligation classified tax-exempt
Fact.Description: The filer's box-2 classification when answered, and false when it is not. ../isComplete requires the answer whenever it can move a dollar (box 11 is $0 and box 2, box 6 or box 10 carries an amount), so reading false here for an unasked question moves nothing.

Fact.Name: Tax-exempt stated interest from Form 1099-OID box 2
Fact.Description: The box 2 amount when box 11 is positive (the form says it is tax-exempt), or when the separate box-2 classification is Yes.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-OID box 6 acquisition premium, $0 when unanswered
Fact.Description: Box 6 (acquisition premium) of this Form 1099-OID as entered, or $0 when the box is not answered. It offsets only the box 11 tax-exempt OID leg in /originalIssueDiscountReports/*/taxExemptOidNetOfAcquisitionPremium.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-OID box 10 bond premium, $0 when unanswered
Fact.Description: Box 10 (bond premium) of this Form 1099-OID as entered, or $0 when the box is not answered. When box 2 is tax-exempt it offsets the tax-exempt stated interest; otherwise it is the taxable bond premium /hasTaxableOIDBondPremium reads.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-OID box 11 tax-exempt OID net of box 6
Fact.Description: Box 11 tax-exempt OID less the box 6 acquisition premium, floored at $0: the tax-exempt OID amount this report carries to Form 1040 line 2a.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-OID tax-exempt box 2 stated interest net of box 10
Fact.Description: The tax-exempt box 2 stated interest (/originalIssueDiscountReports/*/taxExemptStatedInterest) less the box 10 bond premium, floored at $0. When box 2 is not tax-exempt the stated-interest leg is $0 and so is this amount; the premium then stays with the taxable leg.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-OID box 10 bond premium on taxable box 2 interest
Fact.Description: Box 10 bond premium when box 2 is taxable (box 11 is $0 and box 2 is not classified tax-exempt); $0 otherwise, because a tax-exempt box 2 already nets the premium.

Fact.Name: Tax-exempt Form 1099-OID interest for line 2a
Fact.Description: Tax-exempt stated interest from box 2 plus tax-exempt OID from box 11.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-OID tax-exempt interest record is complete
Fact.Description: A blank box 2 or box 11 is $0, as the payer printed it. The one answer the form cannot give is whether a box 11 of $0 means a taxable obligation: when box 11 is $0 and box 2, box 6 or box 10 carries an amount, the filer must classify whether the obligation is tax-exempt, because those three boxes move line 2a or line 2b depending on that answer. Otherwise the record is complete, so box 1, box 8 and every other taxable leg always reach the return.

Fact.Name: At least one Form 1099-OID record is incomplete
Fact.Description: True when a listed Form 1099-OID lacks the tax-exempt classification it needs: box 11 is $0 and box 2, box 6 or box 10 carries an amount that lands on line 2a or line 2b depending on that answer.

Fact.Name: Tax-exempt Form 1099-OID interest total
Fact.Description: Sum of tax-exempt box 2 stated interest and box 11 OID. Complete $0 while the collection is unanswered or empty; not Complete while a listed report still needs its tax-exempt classification (/hasIncompleteOriginalIssueDiscountReports), because that answer decides which line its box 2 is on.

Fact.Name: A Form 1099-OID reports bond premium on taxable box 2 interest
Fact.Description: True when the complete Form 1099-OID collection carries a positive total of /originalIssueDiscountReports/*/taxableBondPremiumForScheduleB; complete-safe false while the collection is unanswered; not Complete while a listed report still needs its tax-exempt classification (/hasIncompleteOriginalIssueDiscountReports). Read by /requiresScheduleBWithoutForm8815.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-OID box 1 original issue discount, $0 when unanswered
Fact.Description: Box 1 (original issue discount for the year) of this Form 1099-OID as entered, or $0 when the box is not answered. It is the OID on a TAXABLE obligation, so it belongs to Form 1040 line 2b through ../taxableInterest and never to line 2a; the tax-exempt counterpart is box 11.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-OID box 8 Treasury OID, $0 when unanswered
Fact.Description: Box 8 (original issue discount on U.S. Treasury obligations) of this Form 1099-OID as entered, or $0 when the box is not answered. It is TAXABLE on the federal return and is reported on Form 1040 line 2b exactly like box 1, which is why it is added to ../taxableInterest and not to the line 2a legs; it is exempt from STATE and local income tax, and the box is exported for the state returns that need to back it out. It is never included in box 1, so adding both boxes double-counts nothing.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-OID box 5 market discount, $0 when unanswered
Fact.Description: Box 5 (market discount) of this Form 1099-OID as entered, or $0 when the box is not answered. It ADDS to reported interest income, and Schedule B line 1 includes accrued market discount that is includible in income. The section 1278(b) ELECTION conditions the box only on a TAXABLE covered security acquired with OID; on a TAX-EXEMPT covered security acquired on or after January 1, 2017 and issued with OID the same box is reported with NO election condition at all (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f1099oid.pdf, page 5 against lines 172-174). So a filled box 5 is NOT by itself proof of an election, and the residue that follows is a named gap in the interest records overlay. It is added for a tax-exempt obligation too - the printed instruction says market discount on a tax-exempt security is includible in TAXABLE income as interest income - so this leg carries no box-11 gate, unlike boxes 6 and 10. Same treatment as the Form 1099-INT counterpart, that form's box 10, in /interestReports/*/bondPremiumAndMarketDiscountAdjustment.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-OID box 6 acquisition premium on taxable OID
Fact.Description: Box 6 acquisition premium when the obligation is TAXABLE (box 11 is $0 AND box 2 is not classified tax-exempt); $0 otherwise. A positive box 11 makes the same box 6 amount the subtrahend of the tax-exempt leg in ../taxExemptOidNetOfAcquisitionPremium and taking it twice would halve the filer's tax-exempt OID and their taxable OID at once. THE SECOND GATE, the box-2 tax-exempt classification, mirrors the three-case box-10 twin ../taxableBondPremiumForScheduleB exactly: it is the PRE-2017 tax-exempt obligation, where the payer "may, but is not required to, report the acquisition premium for a tax-exempt obligation that is a covered security acquired before January 1, 2017, and issued with OID" while box 11 is required only on or after that date, so box 6 is FILLED and box 11 is BLANK on a form carrying no taxable OID at all (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f1099oid.pdf, page 7 against 240-244). Without the gate that premium was subtracted from Form 1040 line 2b -- where it would have offset another payer's interest -- and /hasTaxableOIDAcquisitionPremium went true, forcing Schedule B by the fourth General-Instructions bullet on a return reporting no OID of less than a box 1. This is the "OID Adjustment" Schedule B subtracts below the line-1 subtotal. A box 6 that is FILLED is itself the payer's statement that box 1 and box 8 are GROSS, which is what makes the subtraction permitted; a payer who reported OID net of the premium leaves box 6 blank and this leg resolves $0, which is the instruction's "no reduction ... is permitted" case. NO per-report cap on the subtrahend, deliberately: the return-level GreaterOf $0 on /interestIncome is the only floor, which is the disposition /scheduleBLine1AdjustmentTotal already carries - a box 6 exceeding this payer's own box 1 and box 8 is a data-entry error, and a per-report cap would swallow it.

Fact.Name: Taxable stated interest from Form 1099-OID box 2
Fact.Description: The box 2 qualified stated interest when the obligation is TAXABLE: $0 when box 11 is positive (the form itself then says box 2 is tax-exempt interest and not included in interest income) and $0 when the separate box-2 classification is Yes; the box 2 amount otherwise. Exactly the complement of ../taxExemptStatedInterest, so every dollar of box 2 lands on line 2a or on line 2b and never on both or on neither.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-OID taxable interest for Form 1040 line 2b
Fact.Description: This Form 1099-OID's Schedule B line 1 entry, cents preserved: box 1 plus box 8 plus the taxable part of box 2. The GROSS figure the payer reported, deliberately - the boxes 5, 6 and 10 adjustments are carried BELOW the line-1 subtotal in ../taxableOidAdjustment, which is the mechanic Schedule B prints, so the line-1 entry stays the number the IRS also holds.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-OID taxable interest, the whole-dollar Schedule B line 1 entry
Fact.Description: ../taxableInterest rounded to the whole dollar: the per-payer entry Schedule B Part I line 1 prints. The Schedule B arm of /interestIncome sums these rounded per-payer entries, exactly as it does for /interestReports/*/roundedTaxableInterest, because that is what Schedule B requires; the non-Schedule-B arm sums the unrounded ../taxableInterest and rounds once at the line.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-OID boxes 5, 6 and 10, the signed Form 1040 line 2b adjustment
Fact.Description: The per-report net of the three adjustment boxes that move TAXABLE interest: box 5 market discount ADDS, box 6 acquisition premium on a taxable obligation SUBTRACTS ("OID Adjustment"), box 10 bond premium on taxable box 2 interest SUBTRACTS ("ABP Adjustment"). Carries its own sign, so /interestIncome adds a single term. Applied at the Form 1040 line 2b TOTAL rather than netted into this payer's line-1 entry, which is what Schedule B says to do for the two premium legs and which the Form 1099-INT twin /interestReports/*/taxableBondPremiumAndMarketDiscountAdjustment already does for the same three quantities on that form; the box-5 placement carries the same bounded rounding and MeF-presentation residue that fact names. The tax-exempt uses of boxes 6 and 10 are NOT here - ../taxExemptOidNetOfAcquisitionPremium and ../taxExemptStatedInterestNetOfBondPremium take them when box 11 is positive or box 2 is tax-exempt, and each of the two subtrahends below is $0 in exactly those cases, so no dollar is subtracted twice.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-OID box 4 federal income tax withheld, cents preserved
Fact.Description: Box 4 of this Form 1099-OID, backup withholding, AS REPORTED - cents preserved, not rounded, and $0 when the box is not answered. This is the ADDEND fact /originalIssueDiscountWithholdingUnrounded sums and taxCalculations:/form1099Withholding (Form 1040 line 25b) takes; line 25b adds two or more amounts, and the Form 1040 instructions say to include cents when adding and round off only the total, so this term hands the cents upward and rounds nothing itself. The same shape as /interestReports/*/taxWithheldUnrounded, built that way at birth rather than repaired into it.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-OID box 3 early withdrawal penalty, $0 when unanswered
Fact.Description: Box 3 of this Form 1099-OID, interest or principal forfeited for withdrawing before maturity, as entered or $0 when the box is not answered. IRC 62(a)(9) allows it above the line, so it reaches Schedule 1 line 18 through /originalIssueDiscountEarlyWithdrawalPenaltyTotal - the same treatment the Form 1099-INT counterpart (that form's box 2) already has. It is NOT netted against box 1 or box 2, so it is a deduction on top of the full taxable interest rather than a reduction of it.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-OID taxable interest total, cents preserved
Fact.Description: The Form 1040 line 2b leg of the Form 1099-OID collection when Schedule B is not required: the unrounded sum of every report's ../taxableInterest, rounded once at the line. Complete $0 while the collection is unanswered; not Complete while a listed report still needs its tax-exempt classification (/hasIncompleteOriginalIssueDiscountReports), so a half-answered report never drops out of the line as $0. The membership test is guarded by IsComplete on the collection because a size or membership test over an unanswered collection does not resolve.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-OID taxable interest total, whole-dollar Schedule B entries
Fact.Description: The Form 1040 line 2b leg of the Form 1099-OID collection when Schedule B IS required: the sum of every report's whole-dollar ../roundedTaxableInterest, because Schedule B Part I lists one rounded entry per payer and line 2 totals those entries. Same complete-safe gate as /originalIssueDiscountTaxableInterestTotal.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-OID boxes 5, 6 and 10 adjustment total, signed
Fact.Description: The signed sum of every report's ../taxableOidAdjustment: the "OID Adjustment" and "ABP Adjustment" subtractions Schedule B writes below the line-1 subtotal, net of the box 5 market discount that adds. ONE term, taken by BOTH arms of /interestIncome and by the $1,500 test on /requiresScheduleB, so the printed line, the arm that prints it and the test that chooses the arm can never disagree. Same complete-safe gate as /originalIssueDiscountTaxableInterestTotal, and $0 on every return that lists no Form 1099-OID.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-OID box 4 withholding total, cents preserved
Fact.Description: The Form 1099-OID leg of Form 1040 line 25b: the sum of every report's ../taxWithheldUnrounded, cents preserved. Line 25b rounds once at its own line, so this total rounds nothing - summing per-document rounded box 4s is what the Form 1040 instructions forbid for a line that totals. Complete $0 while the collection is unanswered, so every return that lists no Form 1099-OID has a byte-identical line 25b; not Complete while a listed report still needs its tax-exempt classification (/hasIncompleteOriginalIssueDiscountReports), because a half-answered report completes nothing.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-OID box 3 early withdrawal penalty total
Fact.Description: The Form 1099-OID leg of Schedule 1 line 18: the sum of every report's ../earlyWithdrawalPenaltyOrZero. Added to the Form 1099-INT leg in /schedule1Line18EarlyWithdrawalPenalty. Same complete-safe gate as the other Form 1099-OID totals, so a return that lists no Form 1099-OID has a byte-identical Schedule 1 line 18.

Fact.Name: A Form 1099-OID reports acquisition premium on taxable OID
Fact.Description: True when the complete Form 1099-OID collection carries a positive total of /originalIssueDiscountReports/*/acquisitionPremiumOnTaxableOid: the filer is reporting OID of less than the amount shown in box 1 or box 8, which is the fourth bullet of the Schedule B General Instructions list and requires the schedule with no dollar threshold. Complete-safe false while the collection is unanswered; not Complete while a listed report still needs its tax-exempt classification (/hasIncompleteOriginalIssueDiscountReports). Read by /requiresScheduleB and its cycle-free copy /requiresScheduleBWithoutForm8815. The twin for the box 10 premium leg is /hasTaxableOIDBondPremium, which is the FIFTH bullet; the two bullets are different conditions and each needs its own disjunct.

Fact.Name: Recipient
Fact.Description: Which filer on this return received this Form 1099-OID. SCREEN SPEC: ask "Whose Form 1099-OID is this?" (a filer on the return), first on the Form 1099-OID item, on every Form 1099-OID item. UNANSWERED: the item belongs to neither filer (../belongsToPrimaryFiler and ../belongsToSecondaryFiler both resolve complete-safe false, the same shape form1099Misc.xml ships). WHAT IT FEEDS: ../recipientTin and ../secondaryFilerUsedWithoutMFJ.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-OID belongs to primary filer
Fact.Description: Whether this Form 1099-OID belongs to the primary filer. The IsComplete-first Switch with a literal FALSE default is the same shape form1099Misc.xml ships: an UNANSWERED ../filer resolves complete-safe false instead of inheriting the writable's Placeholder of the primary filer, so an unassigned form is never silently attributed. Read only by ../recipientTin.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-OID belongs to secondary filer
Fact.Description: Whether this Form 1099-OID belongs to the secondary filer. Same shape as the primary arm: an UNANSWERED ../filer resolves complete-safe false. On a single-filer return filers:/secondaryFiler resolves to nothing, so the second IsComplete conjunct decides the Switch to false rather than leaving the fact Incomplete forever -- the MFJ716 completeness lesson, applied at birth. Read by ../recipientTin and ../secondaryFilerUsedWithoutMFJ.

Fact.Name: A spouse's Form 1099-OID on a return that is not joint
Fact.Description: True when this Form 1099-OID names the spouse as its recipient and the return is not married filing jointly. Only a joint return carries both spouses' income, so the spouse's OID, its box 4 withholding and its box 3 penalty have no line on this return. Complete false on a single-filer return and when ../filer is unanswered (../belongsToSecondaryFiler is complete-safe false there).

Fact.Name: A spouse's Form 1099-OID is listed on a return that is not joint
Fact.Description: True when any listed Form 1099-OID names the spouse as its recipient on a return that is not married filing jointly. The return cannot submit until the report is removed or the filing status is joint. Complete false while the collection is unanswered or empty.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-OID recipient's TIN
Fact.Description: The RECIPIENT'S TIN box, as printed (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f1099oid.pdf, page 2). Derived, never asked: the recipient of a Form 1099-OID on this return is one of this return's own filers, so the number is the filer's, resolved from this item's own ../belongsToPrimaryFiler / ../belongsToSecondaryFiler. This is the interest.xml /interestReports/*/recipientTin shape, taken unchanged. NEVER /primaryFiler/tin unconditionally: a spouse's Form 1099-OID would then print the wrong person. UNANSWERED: Incomplete while ../filer is unanswered, which is the honest state. WHAT IT FEEDS: nothing federal. Printed on the Form 1099-OID register and exported for the state and local returns.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-OID payer
Fact.Description: The merged PAYER'S cell, as printed (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f1099oid.pdf, page 2): the payer's name, street address, city or town, state or province, country, ZIP or foreign postal code, and telephone number, in one cell. SCREEN SPEC: ask "Payer's name, address and telephone number as shown on this Form 1099-OID" (free text, several lines), on the payer-identity screen, on every Form 1099-OID item. Help text: the whole block exactly as the issuer, broker or middleman printed it, every line of it. Validation: free text, no length cap, because the cell carries a full postal address and a telephone number. UNANSWERED: complete-safe; nothing on this module reads it as a requirement. WHAT IT FEEDS: nothing federal as a DOLLAR. Boxes 1 and 8 now reach Schedule B Part I line 1, and this payer name is the description printed beside that entry when the schedule is rendered per payer; no computed federal amount depends on it. Stored for the state and local returns and printed on the Form 1099-OID register.

Fact.Name: TIN
Fact.Description: The taxpayer identification number of the payer on this Form 1099-OID, PAYER'S TIN (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f1099oid.pdf, page 2). SCREEN SPEC: ask "Payer's TIN as shown on this Form 1099-OID" (EIN), on the payer-identity screen, on every Form 1099-OID item; never required. Help text: the nine digits the payer printed under PAYER'S TIN. Validation: EIN. UNANSWERED: complete-safe. WHAT IT FEEDS: nothing federal. Stored for the state and local returns and for MeF, and printed on the Form 1099-OID register. This is the interest.xml /interestReports/*/payer/tin shape, taken unchanged.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-OID calendar year

SCREEN SPEC: ask "Calendar year shown on this Form 1099-OID" , on the payer-identity screen, on every Form 1099-OID item; never required. UNANSWERED: complete-safe; nothing on this module reads it as a requirement. WHAT IT FEEDS: nothing federal -- the box identifies the form or the parties to it, and no printed federal line reads it. Stored for the state and local returns and printed on the Form 1099-OID register.

Stored for the state and local returns and printed on the Form 1099-OID register.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-OID 2nd TIN not. box
Fact.Description: The "2nd TIN not." checkbox, as printed on Copy A (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f1099oid.pdf, page 2). SCREEN SPEC: ask "Is the "2nd TIN not." box checked on this Form 1099-OID?" , on the payer-identity screen, on every Form 1099-OID item; never required. Stored for the state and local returns and printed on the Form 1099-OID register.

Fact.Name: FATCA filing requirement, Form 1099-OID
Fact.Description: The FATCA filing requirement checkbox in the left column, as printed (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f1099oid.pdf, page 2). SCREEN SPEC: ask "Is the FATCA filing requirement box checked on this Form 1099-OID?" , on the Form 1099-OID header screen, on every Form 1099-OID item; never required. Help text: the payer checks it when it is a U.S. payer satisfying chapter 4 reporting by filing this Form 1099 (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1099int.pdf, page 6); a checked box can mean the recipient has a Form 8938 filing requirement of its own. Validation: Boolean. UNANSWERED: complete-safe; an unanswered box counts as not checked. WHAT IT FEEDS: /knockoutForm1099OidFatcaAboveForm8938Threshold, which refuses a return with a checked box when the return's Form 8938 threshold answer is above the threshold or unanswered, the same pair the Form 1099-INT box (/interestReports/hasRequiredFactaFilings) reads. Stored for the state and local returns and printed on the Form 1099-OID register.

Fact.Name: A Form 1099-OID FATCA filing requirement box is checked and the return is above the Form 8938 threshold, or that threshold is unanswered
Fact.Description:
Blocks submission when any Form 1099-OID has the FATCA filing requirement box answered checked and the return's Form 8938 threshold answer is ABOVE the threshold or UNANSWERED, read from form8938's return-level pair form8938:/form8938ThresholdAnswered and form8938:/form8938AboveReportingThreshold. The recipient instruction for the box says "You may also have a filing requirement. See the Instructions for Form 8938." The Form 1099-INT box (/interestReports/hasRequiredFactaFilings), the Form 1099-MISC box 13 and the Form 1099-R box refuse on this same pair.
WHAT FILES: a checked box on a return whose specified foreign financial assets are answered below the threshold that applies to the filer. WHAT REFUSES: above the threshold, because a Form 8938 must accompany the return and this dictionary does not produce one (successor: the records contract form8938:/form8938SpecifiedForeignFinancialAssets); and the threshold question unanswered with the box checked, because $0 is not a safe stand-in for an unknown asset total. An unanswered box or an unopened collection short-circuits to false.
SCREEN: "One of your Forms 1099-OID has the FATCA filing requirement box checked. You may need to file Form 8938, Statement of Specified Foreign Financial Assets. Answer the foreign financial assets questions; if your assets are above the Form 8938 threshold, this return cannot be filed here."

Fact.Name: Original issue discount for the year, Form 1099-OID box 1
Fact.Description: Form 1099-OID box 1 as printed (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f1099oid.pdf, page 2): the taxable OID on the obligation for the part of the year the recipient owned it. SCREEN SPEC: ask "Box 1, original issue discount for the year" , on the Form 1099-OID amounts screen, on every Form 1099-OID item; never required. Help text: the payer reports the taxable OID accrued for the part of the year the recipient held the instrument (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1099int.pdf, page 6). Validation: not negative. UNANSWERED: complete-safe; nothing on this module reads it as a requirement. WHAT IT FEEDS: Form 1040 line 2b. It is read through ../originalIssueDiscountOrZero into ../taxableInterest, this report's Schedule B Part I line 1 entry, and reaches /interestIncome through /originalIssueDiscountTaxableInterestTotal and its whole-dollar twin. Box 6 acquisition premium is subtracted below the line-1 subtotal, not from this box. Stored for the state and local returns and printed on the Form 1099-OID register.

Fact.Name: Early withdrawal penalty, Form 1099-OID box 3
Fact.Description: Form 1099-OID box 3 as printed (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f1099oid.pdf, page 2): interest or principal forfeited because of an early withdrawal. SCREEN SPEC: ask "Box 3, early withdrawal penalty" , on the Form 1099-OID amounts screen, on every Form 1099-OID item; never required. Help text: the amount forfeited for withdrawing before maturity (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1099int.pdf, page 6); the Form 1099-INT counterpart is that form's box 2. Validation: not negative. UNANSWERED: complete-safe; nothing on this module reads it as a requirement. WHAT IT FEEDS: Schedule 1 line 18, the penalty on early withdrawal of savings, through ../earlyWithdrawalPenaltyOrZero and /originalIssueDiscountEarlyWithdrawalPenaltyTotal into /schedule1Line18EarlyWithdrawalPenalty, beside the Form 1099-INT box 2 leg. It is NOT netted against box 1 or box 2, so it is a deduction on top of the full taxable interest. Stored for the state and local returns and printed on the Form 1099-OID register.

Fact.Name: Federal income tax withheld, Form 1099-OID box 4
Fact.Description: Form 1099-OID box 4 as printed (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f1099oid.pdf, page 2): the backup withholding the payer took. SCREEN SPEC: ask "Box 4, federal income tax withheld" , on the Form 1099-OID amounts screen, on every Form 1099-OID item; never required. Help text: backup withholding, taken when a recipient does not furnish a TIN (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1099int.pdf, page 6). Validation: not negative. UNANSWERED: complete-safe; nothing on this module reads it as a requirement. WHAT IT FEEDS: Form 1040 line 25b, through ../taxWithheldUnrounded and /originalIssueDiscountWithholdingUnrounded into taxCalculations:/form1099Withholding. Cents are carried upward unrounded; line 25b rounds once at its own line. Stored for the state and local returns and printed on the Form 1099-OID register.

Fact.Name: Market discount, Form 1099-OID box 5
Fact.Description: Form 1099-OID box 5 as printed (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f1099oid.pdf, page 2): the market discount that accrued on a covered security during the year. SCREEN SPEC: ask "Box 5, market discount" , on the Form 1099-OID amounts screen, on every Form 1099-OID item; never required. Help text: the accrued market discount the payer reports for a covered security (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1099int.pdf, page 6); the Form 1099-INT counterpart is that form's box 10. Validation: not negative. UNANSWERED: complete-safe; nothing on this module reads it as a requirement. WHAT IT FEEDS: Form 1040 line 2b. It ADDS, through ../marketDiscountOrZero and ../taxableOidAdjustment, exactly as the Form 1099-INT counterpart /interestReports/*/marketDiscount does on that form. It is added even on a tax-exempt obligation, because market discount on a tax-exempt security is includible in taxable income as interest income. Stored for the state and local returns and printed on the Form 1099-OID register.

Fact.Name: Acquisition premium, Form 1099-OID box 6
Fact.Description: Form 1099-OID box 6 as printed (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f1099oid.pdf, page 2): the acquisition premium amortization that reduces the amount of OID included in income. SCREEN SPEC: ask "Box 6, acquisition premium" , on the Form 1099-OID amounts screen, on every Form 1099-OID item; never required. Help text: a holder who bought the instrument for more than its adjusted issue price amortizes the excess against the OID (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1099int.pdf, page 6). Validation: not negative. UNANSWERED: complete-safe; nothing on this module reads it as a requirement. WHAT IT FEEDS: three ways, not two. Form 1040 line 2a when box 11 is positive (../taxExemptOidNetOfAcquisitionPremium); Form 1040 line 2b when box 11 is $0 and box 2 is NOT classified tax-exempt (../acquisitionPremiumOnTaxableOid, the "OID Adjustment" Schedule B subtracts below the line-1 subtotal), where it also requires Schedule B by the fourth General-Instructions bullet through /hasTaxableOIDAcquisitionPremium; and NEITHER LINE when box 11 is $0 and box 2 IS classified tax-exempt -- the pre-2017 tax-exempt obligation the payer may report a premium for without a box 11 (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f1099oid.pdf, page 7), where the OID the premium reduces is not on this form either, so subtracting it from line 2b would offset a different payer's taxable interest. Stored for the state and local returns and printed on the Form 1099-OID register.

Fact.Name: Description, Form 1099-OID box 7
Fact.Description: Form 1099-OID box 7 as printed (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f1099oid.pdf, page 2): the CUSIP number of the obligation, or a description of it when there is none. SCREEN SPEC: ask "Box 7, description" , on the Form 1099-OID amounts screen, on every Form 1099-OID item; never required. Help text: the payer enters the CUSIP number if any; if there is none, a description of the obligation (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1099int.pdf, page 7). Validation: free text. UNANSWERED: complete-safe; nothing on this module reads it as a requirement. WHAT IT FEEDS: nothing federal -- the box identifies the form or the parties to it, and no printed federal line reads it. Stored for the state and local returns and printed on the Form 1099-OID register.

Fact.Name: Original issue discount on U.S. Treasury obligations, Form 1099-OID box 8
Fact.Description: Form 1099-OID box 8 as printed (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f1099oid.pdf, page 2): the OID on a U.S. Treasury obligation for the part of the year the recipient owned it. SCREEN SPEC: ask "Box 8, original issue discount on U.S. Treasury obligations" , on the Form 1099-OID amounts screen, on every Form 1099-OID item; never required. Help text: Treasury OID is reported separately from box 1 because it is exempt from state and local income tax (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1099int.pdf, page 7). Validation: a dollar amount, WHICH MAY BE NEGATIVE: this box carries no Min $0 limit. The printed instruction to the recipient says "If the number in this box is negative, it represents a deflation adjustment" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f1099oid.pdf, page 7) and the payer instruction says the same in terms -- "The amount in box 8 may be a negative number (for example, if a Treasury Inflation Protected Security has a deflation adjustment for the year)" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1099int.pdf, page 7) -- so a TIPS holder in a deflation year must be able to transcribe the box as printed. A negative box 8 flows through ../treasuryOriginalIssueDiscountOrZero to line 2b as a reduction; the only floor is the return-level GreaterOf $0 on /interestIncome. UNANSWERED: complete-safe; nothing on this module reads it as a requirement. WHAT IT FEEDS: Form 1040 line 2b, through ../treasuryOriginalIssueDiscountOrZero and ../taxableInterest, exactly like box 1 -- Treasury OID is taxable on the FEDERAL return. It is also exactly the number a STATE return needs to back out, because the same OID is exempt from state and local income tax, which is why the box is exported for the state returns. Stored for the state and local returns and printed on the Form 1099-OID register.

Fact.Name: Investment expenses, Form 1099-OID box 9
Fact.Description: Form 1099-OID box 9 as printed (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f1099oid.pdf, page 2). SCREEN SPEC: ask "Box 9, investment expenses" , on the Form 1099-OID amounts screen, on every Form 1099-OID item; never required. Help text: box 9 is filled only by a single-class REMIC (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1099int.pdf, page 7); an ordinary payer's Form 1099-OID leaves it blank. Validation: not negative. UNANSWERED: complete-safe; nothing on this module reads it as a requirement. WHAT IT FEEDS: nothing federal -- the miscellaneous itemized deduction this box once fed is suspended for TY2025 by IRC 67(g), so no federal line reads it. A state that decouples from 67(g) reads it by module-qualified path. Stored for the state and local returns and printed on the Form 1099-OID register.

Fact.Name: Bond premium, Form 1099-OID box 10
Fact.Description: Form 1099-OID box 10 as printed (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f1099oid.pdf, page 2): the bond premium amortization allocable to the interest, for a taxable covered security acquired at a premium. SCREEN SPEC: ask "Box 10, bond premium" , on the Form 1099-OID amounts screen, on every Form 1099-OID item; never required. Help text: a holder who bought a taxable covered security at a premium amortizes it against the interest (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1099int.pdf, page 7); the Form 1099-INT counterpart is that form's box 11. Validation: not negative. UNANSWERED: complete-safe; nothing on this module reads it as a requirement. WHAT IT FEEDS: Form 1040 line 2a when box 2 is tax-exempt (../taxExemptStatedInterestNetOfBondPremium) and Form 1040 line 2b otherwise (../taxableBondPremiumForScheduleB inside ../taxableOidAdjustment, the "ABP Adjustment"). On taxable box 2 interest it also requires Schedule B by the fifth General-Instructions bullet, through /hasTaxableOIDBondPremium. The Form 1099-INT counterpart is that form's box 11. Stored for the state and local returns and printed on the Form 1099-OID register.

Fact.Name: Payer's state, Form 1099-OID box 12, first state row

The printed form carries TWO state rows separated by a dash line -- "Use the state information boxes to report payments for up to two states. Keep the information for each state separated by the dash line." (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1099int.pdf, page 7) -- and that is the printed multiplicity; the other row is ../writablePayerStateAbbreviation2. SCREEN SPEC: ask "Box 12, state (first row)" , on the state-rows screen, on every Form 1099-OID item; never required. Help text: only a form that shows two state rows fills the second; leave it blank otherwise. Validation: one of /statesAndDistrictsOptions. UNANSWERED: complete-safe; nothing on this module reads it as a requirement. WHAT IT FEEDS: nothing federal -- box 12 is a state key and the federal return has no use for which state a payer withheld for. Stored for the state and local returns and printed on the Form 1099-OID register.

Fact.Name: Payer's state, Form 1099-OID box 12, second state row
Fact.Description: Form 1099-OID box 12 as the payer prints it in the SECOND state row: the two-letter abbreviation of a state, one of the fifty states or the District of Columbia (constants:/statesAndDistrictsOptions). The printed form carries TWO state rows separated by a dash line -- "Use the state information boxes to report payments for up to two states. Keep the information for each state separated by the dash line." (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1099int.pdf, page 7) -- and that is the printed multiplicity; the other row is ../writablePayerStateAbbreviation. SCREEN SPEC: ask "Box 12, state (second row)" , on the state-rows screen, on every Form 1099-OID item; never required. Fact.Name: Schedule B line 7a Yes box as the printed Part III carries it
Fact.Description: The line 7a Yes box: the filer has a financial interest in or signature authority over a foreign financial account AND the return must complete Part III at all. The second conjunct is the whole point of this fact. Schedule B has one render gate, /requiresScheduleB, which decides whether the SCHEDULE prints; Part III has its own printed entry test with three conditions, /requiresScheduleBPartIII, and the two genuinely differ - an amortizable-bond-premium filer reporting $400 of interest must use Schedule B and must not complete Part III. Until now the register bound line 7a straight to the intake, so that filer's Schedule B printed an answered Part III he was told not to complete. There is no per-section gate in the register, so the gate is expressed here, in the facts the section's boxes read: when Part III is not required, every box of it resolves false and none is printed.

Fact.Name: Schedule B line 7a No box as the printed Part III carries it
Fact.Description: The line 7a No box: the filer has no foreign financial account AND the return must complete Part III. False on a return that does not have to complete Part III, so neither box of line 7a prints there.

Fact.Name: Schedule B line 7a FinCEN Form 114 Yes box as the printed Part III carries it
Fact.Description: The Yes box of the sub-question under line 7a, which the form asks only of a filer who answered the first question Yes: is that filer required to file FinCEN Form 114. True when Part III is required, the filer has a foreign account, and the attestation is answered Yes; false otherwise, including when the attestation is unanswered.

Fact.Name: Schedule B line 7a FinCEN Form 114 No box as the printed Part III carries it
Fact.Description: The No box of the sub-question under line 7a. CORRECTS A MIS-BINDING: the register bound that box to income:/doesNotHaveForeignAccounts, the negation of the FIRST question, so the filer who has a foreign account and is NOT required to file FinCEN Form 114 - the population the sub-question exists to separate out - printed neither Yes nor No beside it, while the filer with no foreign account at all printed a No beside a question the form does not ask him. This fact is the negation of the sub-question's own attestation, fenced by the first question and by Part III being required at all, and it is false when the attestation is unanswered.
